name: Cape Schanck Lighthouse
address: Cape Schanck Rd, Cape Schanck VIC 3939
signature: A working 1859 lighthouse on the Peninsula's wildest headland — dramatic Bass Strait views and a boardwalk to the cliff edge
editorNote:
Cape Schanck Lighthouse has been operating since 1859 and sits on one of the most exposed headlands on the entire Peninsula — a volcanic basalt promontory with Bass Strait crashing on three sides and views that extend further than seems possible on a clear day.

The boardwalk from the lighthouse down to the cliff edge at Bushranger's Bay is short but spectacular, with wave-cut platforms and blow holes visible at low tide. The lighthouse itself runs guided tours through the lighthouse keeper's cottage — worth the small fee for the historical detail.

No surfing here, and swimming is strongly discouraged. This is a place to stand at the edge and look. Combine with RACV Cape Schanck Resort for lunch or a night nearby.
whyWeGo: Standing at the edge of Cape Schanck — one of the Peninsula's most elemental spots.
ifOnlyOneThing: Walk the boardwalk to the cliff edge and time it with a decent swell. The wave action on the platforms is extraordinary.
pairWith: One Spa at RACV Cape Schanck Resort
